source_window.resource_title: Official public guidance for target title-number discovery
source_window.license: Open Government Licence v3.0 for the guidance page; target-specific index-map results require application and fee

field_evidence.index_map_scope: HM Land Registry states that the index map contains information on land and property that is registered or being registered.
field_evidence.title_number_semantics: The official guidance states that the index map can be used to find the title number of a property that does not appear in a register search.
field_evidence.public_search_restriction: The official guidance explicitly states that users cannot search the map themselves.
field_evidence.submission_requirement: The guidance requires an application form to be completed and sent to HM Land Registry, using an address, a plan, or an Ordnance Survey map reference to identify the land.
field_evidence.fee_requirement: The guidance states that an index-map search costs £8 for an area covering up to 5 registered titles, with additional charges for larger searches.
field_evidence.parcel_promotion_rule: Without a target-specific returned title number and corresponding authoritative parcel/title polygon, no canonical parcel ID, geometry or bbox is promoted.

first_missing_criterion: Verified BUILDING_PRESENT canonical parcel geometry/bbox for this producer. HM Land Registry's official Search the index map guidance provides a title-number discovery route for registered land, but the map cannot be searched directly by the public: an application must be submitted and a fee is charged. Under the required official public/no-login source constraint, this window therefore cannot return the target-specific title number or canonical parcel/title polygon. Local OpenCode or an authorised/paid HM Land Registry workflow must bind the exact target registered-title/index polygon; after that, bind one exact official DEM/LIDAR tile or metadata-index record to the resulting bbox.
exact_blocker: The method was materially changed from HMLR INSPIRE WMS portrayal to HMLR's official Search the index map title-number discovery workflow. The public guidance page is accessible without login, but explicitly states that users cannot search the index map themselves; a submitted application and fee are required to obtain title-number results. Because no target-specific title number or parcel/title geometry is available within the public/no-login window, no canonical parcel ID, geometry or bbox is asserted and spatial join/materialization remains local OpenCode work.
